description.ncbi_summary: The protein encoded by this gene is a guanylyl cyclase found predominantly in photoreceptors in the retina. The encoded protein is thought to be involved in resynthesis of cGMP after light activation of the visual signal transduction cascade, allowing a return to the dark state. This protein is a single-pass type I membrane protein. Defects in this gene may be a cause of X-linked retinitis pigmentosa. [provided by RefSeq, Dec 2008].

uniprot_function.text: Catalyzes the synthesis of cyclic GMP (cGMP) in rod and cone photoreceptors, playing an essential role in phototransduction (PubMed:7777544, PubMed:29515371). Restores cytoplasmic cGMP levels, thereby returning photoreceptor cells to their dark-adapted state via a Ca(2+)-dependent negative feedback loop (PubMed:7777544). Controls the recovery of the photoresponse through interactions with Ca(2+) sensor proteins including GUCA1B (By similarity). Additionally, may participate in the trafficking of membrane-associated proteins to the photoreceptor outer segment membrane (By similarity).
